title: Finite quasi-compact open covers descend along space limits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their fppf sheaves and small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. All indexing sets are small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback over every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, respectively the relative diagonal for a morphism, is quasi-compact. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback over every affine scheme test has affine scheme source [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $S$ with affine transition morphisms, and suppose the fppf sheaf $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ is an algebraic space with its specified projections. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], with open subspaces represented on every scheme test by open subschemes [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finite family of quasi-compact open subspaces $W_1,\ldots,W_n\subset X$ whose union is $X$; $n=0$ is allowed when $X$ is empty. There exist $i\ge i_0$ and quasi-compact open subspaces $W_{a,i}\subset X_i$ such that $W_{a,i}\times_{X_i}X=W_a$ for every $a$, and $\bigcup_{a=1}^n W_{a,i}=X_i$. Every $W_{a,i}$ is quasi-separated, and for $j\ge i$ the inverse images $W_{a,j}$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated with affine transition maps and cover $X_j$.

source.place: Tag 0827 (lemma-descend-opens); finite covering clause needed in the proof of Tag 07SR (lemma-limit-is-scheme), by descent of the empty closed complement, or after an affine atlas by scheme finite-cover descent; Tag 086W (lemma-limit-nonempty).

proof.text: Restrict to the cofinal directed tail $i\ge i_0$: a compatible family on this tail extends uniquely to all indices by choosing an upper bound with each index; independence follows by passing to a common upper bound. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $U_0\to X_{i_0}$ with $U_0$ affine. Put $U_i=X_i\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$. These are affine schemes with affine transitions, by affine base change and composition. Let $U=\varprojlim U_i$ be their scheme limit, which is affine. It represents $X\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$: on any scheme test $T$, both sides consist of a compatible family $T\to X_i$ and a map $T\to U_0$ having the prescribed common map to $X_{i_0}$. This description also identifies every projection. Thus $U\to X$ and $U_i\to X_i$ are surjective etale atlases, and $U\to U_i$ is affine. For any $i$, the affine map $X\to X_i$ is detected on the atlas $U_i\to X_i$, since its pullback is $U\to U_i$. Since $X_i$ is qcqs, affine permanence implies that $X$ is qcqs. The affine schemes $U_i$ and $U$ are qcqs as well.

source.place: Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), atlas construction and (1)-(2); Tag 03H6; affine permanence

proof.text: Every $W_a$ is quasi-separated, since it is a quasi-compact open subspace of the quasi-separated space $X$. The fibre product $E_a=U\times_X W_a$ is therefore qcqs, by qcqs fibre-product permanence applied to $U,W_a,X$. By the definition of an open subspace it is an open subscheme of $U$. Apply scheme open descent to the inverse system $(U_i)$: for each $a$ there are $i_a\ge i_0$ and a quasi-compact open subscheme $E_{a,i_a}\subset U_{i_a}$ whose pullback to $U$ is $E_a$.

source.place: Tag 0827 (lemma-descend-opens), reduction to scheme Tag 01Z4(1); qcqs permanence Tag 073B

proof.text: Choose a common upper bound $k$ of the finitely many $i_a$ and $i_0$; when $n=0$ take $k=i_0$. Set $E_{a,k}=U_k\times_{U_{i_a}}E_{a,i_a}$. The restricted map $E_{a,k}\to E_{a,i_a}$ is a base change of an affine transition map, hence affine and quasi-compact. Thus $E_{a,k}$ is a quasi-compact open of $U_k$, and its inverse image in $U$ is $E_a$. For $j\ge k$ use the same inverse-image construction; affine permanence again gives quasi-compactness of $E_{a,j}$.

source.place: Tag 0827, common-index reduction using affine transitions; scheme Tag 01Z4

proof.text: The inclusion $E_{a,k}\hookrightarrow U_k$ is etale as an open immersion of schemes; composing with the atlas gives a representable etale map to $X_k$. Let $V_{a,k}\subset X_k$ be the image open subspace of the representable etale map $E_{a,k}\to X_k$. It is quasi-compact because $E_{a,k}$ is quasi-compact. The image-open theorem commutes with arbitrary base change. In the pullback to $X$, the source is $E_{a,k}\times_{X_k}X=E_{a,k}\times_{U_k}U=E_a$. Its map to $X$ factors through $W_a$ and is surjective onto $W_a$, since $E_a=U\times_X W_a$ and $U\to X$ is a surjective etale atlas. Consequently $V_{a,k}\times_{X_k}X=W_a$ as open subspaces. This uses image opens, and does not assume that $E_{a,k}$ is invariant under the finite-stage atlas relation.

source.place: Tag 0827 (lemma-descend-opens), made explicit by image opens; Tags 03BZ, 03IR, 03H4, 03H5

proof.text: Put $O_k=\bigcup_a(U_k\times_{X_k}V_{a,k})$, an open subscheme of $U_k$. Its inverse image in $U$ is all of $U$, since the $W_a$ cover $X$. Apply the scheme limit-image-contained-in-open lemma to the affine scheme system $(U_j)_{j\ge k}$ and $O_k$: there is $i\ge k$ with $U_i\times_{U_k}O_k=U_i$. Let $W_{a,i}=X_i\times_{X_k}V_{a,k}$. These opens cover $X_i$: their pullbacks cover the surjective atlas $U_i$, so every point of $X_i$ lies in one of them, and the point/open correspondence identifies their union with $X_i$. They pull back to $W_a$ by the preceding step. When $n=0$, $O_k$ is empty; the very same lemma gives $U_i$ empty, hence $X_i$ empty, as required.

source.place: Finite covering step implicit in Tag 07SR (lemma-limit-is-scheme); scheme Tag 01Z4(3), via Tag 01Z3

proof.text: Each $V_{a,k}$ is quasi-separated because it is a quasi-compact open subspace of the quasi-separated $X_k$. For every $j\ge k$, the map $X_j\times_{X_k}V_{a,k}\to V_{a,k}$ is affine, being the base change of $X_j\to X_k$. Affine permanence therefore makes this open qcqs. In particular this applies at $i$ and at all $j\ge i$. For $j'\ge j\ge i$ the transition $W_{a,j'}\to W_{a,j}$ is the base change of $X_{j'}\to X_j$, hence affine. Finally the pullbacks of the covering union $\bigcup_a W_{a,i}=X_i$ cover $X_j$: a point over $X_i$ lies in the inverse image of whichever $W_{a,i}$ contains its image. The point/open correspondence makes this an equality of open subspaces.

lean.note: Finite covers use unions of point images, not sectionwise subfunctor unions. The later-stage clause includes j = i, so it also asserts quasi-compactness, absolute quasi-separatedness and covering for the descended family itself. Restricted transitions are uniquely fixed by commutation with the monic open inclusions.
